name: Soft Hackle Sowbug
imitates: A sowbug (aquatic isopod), the staple tailwater food item; the orange thread glowing through the dubbing is a Bighorn River trick that fish seem to prefer.
recipe: UNI 8/0 fluorescent fire orange or red

steps.text: Start the thread an eye length behind the eye and wrap a smooth base to the bend, then back to the start so the shank has an even orange layer.
Dub a thin strand of cinnamon dubbing and wrap a single layer from the bend up to the front of the shank.
Wrap the remaining dubbing back over the front two thirds and forward again to build a slightly tapered body, ending with bare thread at the back of the hackle spot.
Pick a hen feather with barbs about shank length, strip the fluff, and tie it in by the butt at the front of the body with the concave side toward the shank.
Pull the feather up in hackle pliers and stroke the barbs back toward the rear of the stem, just enough for a couple of turns.
Wrap the hen feather forward for about two turns, one directly in front of the other, and tie it off behind the eye.
Clip the leftover feather tip as close to the hook as you can.
Push the hackle fibers back along the body with your thread hand.
Hold the fibers back from the rear and wrap a small thread head in front of them so they sweep into a neat collar.
Build a smooth orange thread head, whip finish, and add a small drop of head cement. The finished fly.
